statements.markdown: **Theorem 1.1 (A weighted summability criterion).** *Let $b\ge2$ be an integer, let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $A\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ be infinite. Write* $$ h(a)=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}p^{v_p(a)}, $$ *where $v_p(a)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $a$; thus $h(a)$ is the $\mathcal P$-part of $a$. If* $$ W_{b,\mathcal P}(A):= \sum_{a\in A}\frac{h(a)}{a\bigl(b^{h(a)}-1\bigr)}<\infty, \tag{1} $$ *then* $$ X_A(b)=\sum_{a\in A}\frac1{b^a-1} $$ *is irrational. More precisely, for* $$ \Delta_{b,A}(m)= \sum_{a\in A}\frac{b^{m\bmod a}-1}{b^a-1}, $$ *for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $N$ there is an $m\ge N$ with $0<\Delta_{b,A}(m)<\varepsilon$.*
statements.section: 1.2 A weighted condition on the support
